Build notes / rendering upgrade

RINK RUCKUS!
THREE r186.

September 29, 2026 · GPT-6 Astra Pro · 2.0.0-r186

Delivery limit: The initial delivery file does not contain the Three.js library bytes. That file needs Internet access once. Use Save Offline Copy after the engine loads. That new file includes all downloaded JavaScript, Basis WASM, assets, and audio. The initial file is not the offline-first delivery requested in the original brief.
Launch and package state

Open this HTML in a browser. The first-launch edition gets files from one fixed commit in the official Three.js repository. No server or installation is needed. The saved offline edition uses only embedded data and local Blob URLs. It stops with an error if an embedded dependency is missing. It does not silently switch to a custom renderer.

Use Hit the Ice to start the existing three-period match. Controls, touch input, lineups, unlocks, save key, music, and rules remain from version 1. Options include a local GLB prop importer and an offline-export button. A GLB import replaces the sideline trophy only. The file is included in the next offline export.

Local records use rink-ruckus-v1. Local-file storage and fullscreen can be restricted by browser policy. Records are not copied between HTML files by the export control. Keep using the same file location to retain local records where the browser permits it.

Renderer and lighting

The renderer is WebGPURenderer from three/webgpu. It uses AgXToneMapping, SRGBColorSpace, and PCFShadowMap. Three.js selects WebGL2 when WebGPU is not available. Both paths use the same scene and materials. A ?backend=webgl2 URL option selects WebGL2 for a comparison.

The engine is pinned to r186 commit 9b4a2ac29c63ccb43fd51c5661f2f873ac2c39b8. The offline packer checks SHA-256 digests when Web Crypto is available. The code checks THREE.REVISION === '186'. It does not use a floating latest version. Import-map entries point to local Blob modules after the engine graph has loaded.

An original 512 × 256 Radiance HDR environment is embedded. RGBELoader reads it. A Three.js PMREMGenerator filters it for image-based lighting. The source HDR and the temporary generator are then disposed. In r186, RGBELoader is a deprecated wrapper for HDRLoader. The requested class is retained. Its warning is expected.

One directional sun supplies direct light and shadows. The shadow camera fits the arena caster bounds in light space. Its center snaps to shadow texels. The large floor slab does not expand the fitted bounds. The fit is recalculated when the shadow size changes. No ambient, hemisphere, point, or extra imported lights are added.

TSL RenderPipeline and cost controls

The output graph is linear HDR scene → optional half-resolution bloom → AgX → sRGB → FXAA → screen. The code uses the r186 RenderPipeline, TSL pass, renderOutput, and TSL effect nodes. outputColorTransform is false because the graph applies the output transform before FXAA. The tone-mapped intermediate target uses 8-bit color to reduce memory and bandwidth. It does not apply tone mapping twice. There is no EffectComposer, ShaderMaterial, or onBeforeCompile patch.

PresetResolution limitShadows / effectsSimulation budget
HighUp to 1.5× CSS pixels; 4.2 MP2048 PCF; 4× scene MSAA; FXAA; half-resolution bloom160 particles; 6 fixed steps per frame
BalancedUp to 1× CSS pixels; 2.2 MP1024 PCF; FXAA; no bloom passes64 particles; 4 fixed steps per frame
Auto: low-cost stateUp to 0.75× CSS pixels; 0.95 MP512 PCF; FXAA; no bloom passes28 particles; 3 fixed steps per frame

Auto selects a cost state from measured frame intervals. It does not check device names. A delay and hysteresis prevent rapid changes. The physics time step remains 1/60 second in every preset. Rendering interpolates between fixed steps. Under severe overload, the inherited step cap can drop excess accumulated time.

The arena uses one merged static geometry draw. Players, puck, and effects use a reusable typed stream and one dynamic geometry draw. Only the used vertex range is uploaded. Three bounded effect graphs are cached. Inactive full-screen buffers shrink to release memory. The original low-poly shapes and contact discs remain. The imported prop uses standard glTF PBR materials and packed ORM maps.

Asset pipeline and initialization order

GLTFLoader has both KTX2Loader and MeshoptDecoder attached. Basis transcoder JavaScript and WASM are part of the dependency package. KTX2 uses at most two workers. The renderer initializes before detectSupport(renderer). Basis setup and MeshoptDecoder.ready finish before models load.

Packed ORM uses R: occlusion, G: roughness, B: metalness. Data maps use NoColorSpace. GLTFLoader retains the texture coordinates declared by the model. The importer does not force all maps onto a second UV set. Base-color and emissive color handling remains with GLTFLoader.

The embedded club trophy is a real GLB with one packed ORM PNG. It is an uncompressed test asset. It is not presented as a successful Basis or Meshopt compressed-data test. The local importer accepts self-contained GLB files up to 24 MB, with bounded mesh and vertex counts. Draco is not enabled. Imported lights and cameras are removed to preserve the rink lighting and camera.

Startup awaits the renderer, decoder setup, HDR loading, PMREM shader preparation, model parsing, and scene shader compilation. A pipeline warm-up occurs before setAnimationLoop. The loop calls synchronous RenderPipeline.render() only after initialization. There is no async frame overlap. Quality changes and model imports share a serial configuration queue. Rendering and game time pause during reconfiguration. Hidden pages do not render. Device loss and startup errors produce visible messages.

Old geometry, imported textures, ImageBitmaps, render targets, workers, the environment target, and Blob URLs have disposal paths. Library source licenses remain in the saved engine modules. The Three.js LICENSE file is also stored in the engine package.

Selected-level source checklist → implementation
Source elementWhere it appears in this slice
Kendo practice match; club at riskBriefing, original Kunio/Tōru dialogue, opponent introduction, and Kaori-style results newspaper. The earlier dodgeball match is summarized, not replayed.
Nekketsu indoor rinkOne bounded ice arena, two goals, benches, spectator stands, and visible trash cans. Pregame → rink → intermissions → final newspaper are all linked transitions.
Three skaters plus goalkeeperEach side has a forward, winger, defender, goalkeeper, and one reserve. Four unique assignments; intermission substitutions; goalkeeper grades influence catching.
Five hockey-club playersKunio, Yōichi, Hideki, Tsuyoshi, and Masashi are selectable. Their power, speed, weight, and goalkeeper grades are used by the simulation.
Kendo opponentsTōru, Takahiro, Makoto, and Tomonori start; Aguri is the reserve. The team uses bamboo shockwaves, not character super shots.
Skating, dash, U-turn, jumpMomentum-based motion, directional bursts, sharp turns, stamina consumption, jumping collisions, and pose changes.
Passes and aerial setupsGround pass, held flip pass, self-pop, aerial volley, and short first-time shooting window. Open-lane support AI and automatic receiver selection.
Power-limited, timed super shotsVisible charge window, power drain, overcharge stun and puck loss. All five signatures: penetrating Nuts; stationary Dejected trap; small Compressed; orbit/pause/fire Rotating; wall-bouncing One-cushion.
Stick and body attacksTrip, long airborne stick, dash spin, airborne dash machine swing, shoulder check, and air punch. Weight and uniform armor affect knockback/damage.
Anger and trash-can penaltiesRepeated received hits trigger character-duration anger. Three connected angry attacks penalize the offender until an opposing goal releases them.
Goalkeeper play; no offsideAI positioning, catches, rebounds and distribution; optional direct control and a timed diving catch. No icing or offside interruptions.
Kendo uniform rewardA victory saves the kit. Equip it on results or in the locker room; visual armor, attack/defense changes and the jumping shockwave all become usable in a rematch.
Items, quests, upgrades, encountersThe uniform is the match’s equipment reward; there are no invented source quests, shops, pickups, or extra encounter rooms. Skill challenges below are explicit additions.
New assets and other changes

New: the r186 renderer and post graph; a generated HDR environment; a gold club-trophy GLB; its packed ORM PNG; linear vertex-color conversion; reusable typed geometry storage; local GLB import; engine checksums; the first-launch packer and offline export; revised diagnostics and error handling.

Unchanged: the original match, title layout, source checklist, dialogue, controls, AI, custom fixed-step hockey physics, progression key, and generated audio. This upgrade does not replace the custom physics with Rapier. It does not replace the generated sounds with source-game recordings. It does not claim those original requirements are now met. Vite was not run in the restricted build environment.

Asset credits and audio manifest

Rink Studio HDR: original procedural Radiance RGBE environment, 512 × 256, generated by GPT-6 Astra Pro on September 29, 2026. Club Trophy: original faceted GLB and 16 × 16 packed ORM PNG, generated on the same date. All other faceted shapes and UI remain from the supplied game.

The unchanged audio-manifest contains generated placeholders, not original-game rips: music (After-School Overtime), hit, shot, pass, jump, whistle, super, goal, menu, pickup, penalty, charge, slide. All use embedded WAV data. Original source-recording requests from Zophar and Sounds Resource remain unmet. No new claim of permission to redistribute source-game media is made.

Three.js: Three.js authors, MIT. Meshoptimizer: Arseny Kapoulkine and contributors, MIT. Basis Universal: Binomial and contributors, Apache 2.0. KTX2 and Zstandard support files retain their source notices. No game ROM, source-game sprite, font file, or proprietary source code is added. Imported local models retain their owners’ rights.

Content intentionally outside the slice

The earlier dodgeball opener, Baseball Club, Yurigaoka, Hanazono, roller-skate match, Shirogane match, national tournament, other arenas and hazards, later recruits, other uniforms, passwords and secrets, four-player multiplayer, co-op, and a full campaign are outside this one-match slice. There is no network play. No external campaign progression is implied by the ending.

Verification limits and known issues

The build environment blocked package downloads. Thus the official Three.js and Basis bytes could not be embedded before delivery. This is a first-launch package, not an initially self-contained game. It does not work offline until the engine is loaded and the user saves an offline copy.

The new WebGPU and WebGL2 scenes could not be executed in this environment. Real rendering, compressed-model decoding, exact visual appearance, and physical-device frame rate are not verified. The code is based on the pinned r186 source, but API-level checks are not a substitute for a native GPU run. An uncaught renderer error stops the loop and shows an error screen.

Validation completed on September 29, 2026. 17 packaging checks and 23 gameplay-harness checks passed in Chromium. Packaging checks used small fixture modules, an inline browser page, and a test SHA-256 bridge. The saved fixture package ran with zero HTTP or HTTPS requests. These checks did not load the real Three.js library or run real Basis or Meshopt decoders. Gameplay checks used the preserved game code with a renderer test double. A complete regulation match reached results after 10,810 fixed physics steps and two intermissions. Keyboard and two-finger touch input, all five home super shots, ground and lofted passes, checking, lineup changes, uniform rewards, and win/loss/draw screens passed. Static and dynamic geometry was finite. The dynamic vertex buffer was reused. Node syntax checks passed for the renderer, combined game module, and package bootstrap. The original audio manifest was retained. Audio output was not re-tested. Native WebGPU and WebGL2 rendering, real compressed-asset decoding, visual quality, device frame rates, native Web Crypto, direct-file launch, and the browser's download action were not verified. Browser policy blocked file and localhost navigation. The code that creates the exported HTML was tested with fixture dependencies. Package downloads were blocked in the build environment.

The old version’s software-renderer test report is historical. It is not evidence for the new renderer. The supplied browser blocks file navigation. Direct-file launch and the native browser download action are not verified. Current limits also include the original custom physics and generated audio, local-file storage restrictions, a small portrait play area, and browser fullscreen restrictions. The renderer uses CPU-updated batched character geometry, not GPU skeletal animation. It has no GPU-time benchmark or universal performance guarantee.
